last_session.detail: The party assumed the treasure lies at one of the marked locations. All the land around Brandonsford was unknown to them.
last_session.text: The party arrived in Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map whose marked places they did not recognize.

last_session.detail: Reginald said the Clurichen is up to no good and that wherever it goes, they should stay away.
last_session.text: Reginald the frog warned Dr. Uriah that a trickster Clurichen comes into town from the riverbanks each night.

last_session.detail: Dunk split from the party to scavenge, preferring solitude to the inns. Gill's legend: Sir Brandon met a fairy in the woods who gave him a magic sword. He and his friends killed a dragon that had terrorized the town for weeks, and the town was named after him. They were knighted, then all left, and Brandon died. That dragon was dragged through town and ripped apart hundreds of years ago. Gill assumes the current dragon is a different one and does not know where dragons come from. Gill saw the current dragon, which wanted nothing to do with him, and sent his three sons after it. Dunk asked to sleep in the barn and think over the offer. They drank from Gill's still while Gill shared gossip.
last_session.text: Dunk spent the night drinking with Farmer Gill, who told him the legend of Sir Brandon the dragonslayer.

last_session.detail: Eric offered 1000 gold to whoever kills the dragon and drags its body into town, calling it the first of many problems. Eric said George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses down, lost an arm to the dragon and described it as a small black dragon. George might show up at the tavern tonight. The duel followed Eric defending George's account. Eric did not accept the challenge, only saying Sir Phidipaldi was more skilled at adventure.
last_session.text: Eric the Reeve offered a bounty for the dragon, and Sir Phidipaldi slapped him with a glove and challenged him to a duel.

last_session.detail: Dr. Uriah brought Ned a Fox Tail Brew. Ned recognized Uriah as a Dagonite. Uriah claimed to be a scholar of folk remedies and lore seeking work with his crew. Ned asked 100 gold for the week. For a night of at least ten kills, Ned would keep the fee but pay back 5 gold per kill if he could do what he wanted with the victims.
last_session.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp, offered to hire on with Dr. Uriah, who said he would think about it.

last_session.detail: Quinn says his good stock is gone each morning, with half the glasses empty or knocked over, so he waters down what little he has. He believes Bentley steals it because Bentley's Fox Tail Brew is so popular. Sir Phidipaldi offered to help Quinn get back at Bentley. Quinn offered 100 gold and proposed a fake shipment.
last_session.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn catch whoever empties the Golden Egg's good ale each night.
